images.title: A border of twelve tiles
images.purpose: Show the example of the concept: two shapes taking turns in a row, 6 squares and 6 triangles, with the same two shapes meeting at every join.
images.composition: One row of twelve tiles, squares and triangles in turn, with a dot at each of the eleven joins and the count written below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP CENTRE: the title A border of 12 tiles, bold 44 px dark #1F2937, centred at x 728 and y 130. THE BORDER: exactly 12 tiles in one row on the baseline y 440, each with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px), the tiles taking turns and starting with a square: odd tiles are SQUARES of 100 by 100 px filled teal #0072B2, even tiles are EQUILATERAL TRIANGLES with a base of 100 px and a height of 87 px, pointing up, filled amber #E69F00. In order from the left: square 1: x 128 to 228, y 340 to 440; triangle 2: corners (228, 440), (328, 440), (278, 353); square 3: x 328 to 428, y 340 to 440; triangle 4: corners (428, 440), (528, 440), (478, 353); square 5: x 528 to 628, y 340 to 440; triangle 6: corners (628, 440), (728, 440), (678, 353); square 7: x 728 to 828, y 340 to 440; triangle 8: corners (828, 440), (928, 440), (878, 353); square 9: x 928 to 1028, y 340 to 440; triangle 10: corners (1028, 440), (1128, 440), (1078, 353); square 11: x 1128 to 1228, y 340 to 440; triangle 12: corners (1228, 440), (1328, 440), (1278, 353). So there are 6 squares and 6 triangles, and each tile touches the next one at the corner on the baseline. JOINS: exactly 11 reddish purple #CC79A7 dots of 22 px across, one on the baseline at each place where two neighbouring tiles touch, at (x, y) = (228, 440), (328, 440), (428, 440), (528, 440), (628, 440), (728, 440), (828, 440), (928, 440), (1028, 440), (1128, 440), (1228, 440). TEXT BELOW: at y 540, centred at x 728, the text At every join, a square and a triangle meet (40 px, dark #1F2937); at y 660, centred at x 728, the bold dark text 6 squares + 6 triangles = 12 tiles (64 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame, no numbers on the tiles.
labels: At every join, a square and a triangle meet
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of tiles or dots that differs from the numbers stated in the spec, or two squares or two triangles side by side
a gap between a square and the baseline, a triangle pointing down, or any number written on a tile
images.takeaway: Tiles that take turns repeat in the same order, so the same two shapes meet at every join.
images.description: A border of twelve tiles in a row, squares and triangles taking turns, with a dot at each join.
images.context: Concept image for Two Shapes Take Turns. It follows the idea of the patterns with more than one shape in your maths book (shapes that repeat in the same order) and uses the concept's own border of 12 tiles.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to touch each dot and name the two tiles that meet there. The slip to watch: thinking different shapes can meet at different joins in a border that takes turns.

image_decisions.why: The border of 12 tiles shows squares and triangles taking turns, with a square and a triangle meeting at every join.
